nodes.label: C-3-01
nodes.text: A conforming reader at any level MUST ignore constructs it does not understand rather than reject the document containing them (this is what lets levels and versions advance without breaking anyone).

nodes.label: C-3.1-01
nodes.text: The key is **informative, not a negotiation**: readers MUST accept any `0.x` value and apply the standing ignore-unknown rules (§13.1) to whatever they find.

nodes.label: C-3.2-01
nodes.text: **Readers MUST NOT gate any behaviour on any of them** — not parsing, not feature selection, not trust.

nodes.label: C-3.2-02
nodes.text: `generator` nonetheless carries real weight, which is why publishers SHOULD emit it in the form `name/version` (e.g. `blygger-studio/0.4.0`): the manifest is a file the protocol requires to be public, so `generator` is the only census of the ecosystem that exists without anyone registering anything.

nodes.label: C-3.2-03
nodes.text: It is the client's name, never the protocol's: a client rename is not a protocol change and MUST NOT be read as one.

nodes.label: C-4-01
nodes.text: The surface is strictly origin-relative: no protocol construct may assume any particular path component, and readers MUST NOT infer anything from the mount path.

nodes.label: C-4-02
nodes.text: The file names *within* the surface (`blyg.json`, `feed.xml`, `items/…`) are protocol-fixed and MUST NOT vary per deployment — a known manifest filename at an arbitrary origin is what keeps free mounting discoverable (a reader handed any base URL fetches `blyg.json` relative to it).

nodes.label: C-4-03
nodes.text: Publishers MUST serve:

nodes.label: C-4-04
nodes.text: Publishers MAY additionally serve:

nodes.label: C-4-05
nodes.text: `blogroll.opml`  ;  Curated blogroll (OPTIONAL)  ;  §11

nodes.label: C-4-06
nodes.text: *(the URL named by the manifest's `webmention` key)*  ;  Webmention endpoint (OPTIONAL; the protocol's only dynamic surface)  ;  §15

nodes.label: C-4-07
nodes.text: Publishers SHOULD additionally serve human-readable HTML (a feed page, item permalink pages); their form is presentation, not protocol, except where noted (§5.8, §8.4, §10.5, §15.1).

nodes.label: C-4-08
nodes.text: The entire surface MUST be servable as plain static files.

nodes.label: C-4-09
nodes.text: `items/{id}.json` MUST return 404 for unknown ids and never-published drafts, and MUST return 200 permanently once the item has ever been published — including after withdrawal.

nodes.label: C-4-10
nodes.text: `items/{id}/v{n}.json` MUST return 404 unless version n of item id is pinned, and MUST return 200 permanently once it is (§8).

nodes.label: C-4-11
nodes.text: Public JSON and XML responses SHOULD be served with permissive CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`); cross-origin reading by other clients depends on it.

nodes.label: C-4-12
nodes.text: A publisher MUST NOT write local time into any protocol surface; time-zone display is a presentation concern of each client.

nodes.label: C-5-01
nodes.text: Threads additionally carry `transclusions` (§10.3) and MAY carry `stub_of` (§10.6).

nodes.label: C-5-02
nodes.text: Any item MAY carry `forked_from` (§5.6) and `generated` (§5.7).

nodes.label: C-5.1-01
nodes.text: `id` MUST be 128 random bits encoded as 26 characters of lowercase Crockford base32 (alphabet `0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz`, no padding), generated from a cryptographically strong source.

nodes.label: C-5.1-02
nodes.text: Ids are permanent identity: they MUST NOT change across versions, withdrawal, or return.

nodes.label: C-5.1-03
nodes.text: `content_hash` MUST be `"sha256:" + hex(SHA-256(content_md as UTF-8))`, computed per published version.

nodes.label: C-5.2-01
nodes.text: A note that quotes the prior version's text is a diff by another name and leaks exactly what withholding protects, so where the prior version is unpinned a note MUST NOT reproduce it.

nodes.label: C-5.2-02
nodes.text: `updated` MUST equal the latest changelog entry's `at`.

nodes.label: C-5.2-03
nodes.text: **`content_html` is self-contained** (revision of 2026-10-03, decision #53): every URL in it — media, links, the anchors `[[id]]` renders to, anything an `href` or `src` can carry — MUST be absolute.

nodes.label: C-5.2-04
nodes.text: Readers MAY resolve a relative URL against the document's origin on import as a defensive measure and MUST NOT depend on one being present.

nodes.label: C-5.3-01
nodes.text: Readers MUST treat unknown kinds as unknown constructs: ignore the item, don't reject the feed or archive containing it.

nodes.label: C-5.3-02
nodes.text: Fragments: publishers SHOULD cap `content_md` at 2,000 characters (RECOMMENDED studio-enforced cap: 1,000).

nodes.label: C-5.3-03
nodes.text: Enforcement is publisher-side only — readers MUST NOT reject long fragments.

nodes.label: C-5.3-04
nodes.text: The feed's `<title>` element is derived (§7); a leading markdown heading in `content_md` is content, not a title, and readers MUST NOT extract one.

nodes.label: C-5.4-01
nodes.text: `media` entries carry `url` (relative to the origin or absolute), `mime`, and SHOULD carry `alt`.

nodes.label: C-5.4-02
nodes.text: Media objects are immutable once published: a media URL MUST always serve the same bytes.

nodes.label: C-5.5-01
nodes.text: `author` is OPTIONAL, per-item, **client-asserted, and opaque**:

nodes.label: C-5.5-02
nodes.text: `name` (display string) is RECOMMENDED, `url` OPTIONAL; **any additional members are permitted and unspecified** — they are the client's private authorspace grammar (local ids, OAuth subjects, wallet signatures, …).

nodes.label: C-5.5-03
nodes.text: Readers MUST accept any object here and MUST NOT reject an item over its `author` contents.

nodes.label: C-5.5-04
nodes.text: It is scoped to `(origin, value)`: equal values from different origins MUST NOT be treated as the same entity.

nodes.label: C-5.5-05
nodes.text: Clients that store or re-emit item JSON MUST carry `author` verbatim, never synthesized or rewritten.

nodes.label: C-5.6-01
nodes.text: *(Reserved at 0.1 and 0.2; defined at 0.3.)* An item MAY carry a top-level `forked_from`: a reference (§5.9) to the **pinned** version of another item from which this item's first draft was copied.

nodes.label: C-5.6-02
nodes.text: `origin` is REQUIRED, even when it is the publisher's own — a citation is absolute.

nodes.label: C-5.6-03
nodes.text: The referenced version MUST be pinned at its origin, i.e. fetchable as `{origin}items/{id}/v{n}.json`.

nodes.label: C-5.6-04
nodes.text: Publishers SHOULD check this at publish time with one conditional fetch, and SHOULD refuse to publish on **evidence** that the promise is not kept — a 4xx, or a 200 that is not that pinned version.

nodes.label: C-5.6-05
nodes.text: A network failure, timeout, or 5xx is evidence of nothing; refusing to publish an author's own words because a stranger's host is down would hand third parties a veto, so publishers SHOULD proceed with a warning instead.

nodes.label: C-5.6-06
nodes.text: Lineage is fixed when the item is created and is **immutable**: it never changes across versions, and a client MUST NOT offer a way to add, retarget, or clear it after the fact.

nodes.label: C-5.6-07
nodes.text: Lineage across origins is a remote reference and SHOULD send a mention (§15.2), whose relation is `fork`.

nodes.label: C-5.6-08
nodes.text: Readers MUST NOT infer that a fork still resembles its source.

nodes.label: C-5.7-01
nodes.text: What the wire gains is generation's **provenance shadow**: a publisher whose version contains machine-generated prose SHOULD disclose it via an OPTIONAL top-level `"generated"` array, parallel to `transclusions`, one entry per generated span in document order:

nodes.label: C-5.7-02
nodes.text: It MAY be empty, meaning **no sources declared**: pure instructed generation, or generation whose sources the publisher cannot name.

nodes.label: C-5.7-03
nodes.text: `model` and `at` are RECOMMENDED.

nodes.label: C-5.7-04
nodes.text: A span MAY be the whole body.

nodes.label: C-5.7-05
nodes.text: The array MUST NOT carry instruction text or any other pre-generation authoring state — instructions are studio-private, permanently.

nodes.label: C-5.7-06
nodes.text: A publisher that knows a span is machine-generated SHOULD disclose it regardless of who ran the model; the construct exists so that disclosure is always possible.

nodes.label: C-5.7-07
nodes.text:
Publishers additionally disclose generated spans in the rendered HTML: the renderer MUST wrap each generated span in `content_html` as `…` (inline output) or `
…
` (block output).

nodes.label: C-5.8-01
nodes.text: *(New in 0.3.)* An item document MAY carry `"page"`: the **origin-relative URL of the item's human-readable permalink**, resolved against the origin (`"page": "t/7c9wk2mhq0v3xj8tn5rzfd41bg/"`).

nodes.label: C-5.8-02
nodes.text: Readers SHOULD use `page` when present, and MAY fall back to the reference convention (`f/{id}/` for fragments, `t/{id}/` for threads) when it is absent.

nodes.label: C-5.8-03
nodes.text: A permalink page SHOULD carry `<link rel="alternate" type="application/json" href="{origin}items/{id}.json">`.

nodes.label: C-5.8-04
nodes.text: **`page` SHOULD be stable for the life of the item** (revision of 2026-10-03, decision #56).

nodes.label: C-5.8-05
nodes.text: A publisher that must move a page SHOULD serve a redirect from the old path.

nodes.label: C-5.8-06
nodes.text: Readers MAY refresh `page` from the item document on any fetch (the staleness check fetches it anyway), and a frozen `cited.url` naming the old path remains correct: it names what was seen.

nodes.label: C-5.9-01
nodes.text: It is REQUIRED in `forked_from` and `stub_of` (a citation is absolute) and OPTIONAL in `transclusions[]`, where omission means own-origin, so that every 0.2 thread document stays valid unchanged.

nodes.label: C-5.9-02
nodes.text: A reference MAY additionally carry the human half of a citation, `cited`, defined next — and nothing else.

nodes.label: C-5.9-03
nodes.text: A reference MAY therefore carry an OPTIONAL `cited` object: the label the citing publisher saw when it made the reference.

nodes.label: C-5.9-04
nodes.text: `retrieved` is REQUIRED whenever `cited` is present — a citation without a date is not a citation.

nodes.label: C-5.9-05
nodes.text: `source` (the target blyg's title as seen), `author` (the target's own `author.name`, passed through under §5.5), `excerpt` (a short caption; publishers SHOULD cap it near 200 characters) and `url` (the target's page as it stood) are OPTIONAL.

nodes.label: C-5.9-06
nodes.text: Mention verification (§15.4) reads the three identity members alone and MUST NOT consult `cited`.

nodes.label: C-5.9-07
nodes.text: Readers MUST NOT present it as verified or as the target's current state, MUST NOT bake it into `content_html`, and a reader that ignores it entirely remains conformant.

nodes.label: C-6.1-01
nodes.text: The `blogroll` key is OPTIONAL: an origin-relative path, canonically `"blogroll.opml"`, present only when the publisher serves a non-empty blogroll (§11).

nodes.label: C-6.1-02
nodes.text: The `webmention` key (new in 0.3) is OPTIONAL: the URL of the publisher's Webmention endpoint, origin-relative allowed, present only when the publisher receives mentions (§15.1); a static export omits it.

nodes.label: C-6.1-03
nodes.text: `level` and `generator` are informative (§3.2), and so is **`generator_url`** (new in 0.3): OPTIONAL, one absolute URL to the client software's canonical source repository or home page, baked in by the client's author beside `generator` (the precedent is Atom's generator `uri`).

nodes.label: C-6.1-04
nodes.text: Publishers SHOULD emit it; readers MUST NOT gate on it; its absence means only that nothing was stated.

nodes.label: C-6.1-06
nodes.text: A registry MAY require a client source as a condition of *listing*; that is its business, not conformance.

nodes.label: C-7-01
nodes.text: The window SHOULD be bounded (RECOMMENDED: 50 entries).

nodes.label: C-7-02
nodes.text: A feed entry for an older publish event keeps its own `blyg:version` and note, but its `<description>` MUST carry the *latest* version's HTML.

nodes.label: C-7-03
nodes.text: RSS requires the element, so publishers MUST emit one, and it MUST NOT be read back as an item field.

nodes.label: C-7-04
nodes.text: The RECOMMENDED derivation, which the reference client uses, is the publish event's changelog note followed by an em-dash and a short excerpt of the content (`note — excerpt`), or the excerpt alone when there is no note; a withdrawal entry's title is the literal `withdrawn`.

nodes.label: C-7-05
nodes.text: Its earlier publish events MUST be dropped from the window (with content withheld they would render as empty noise under the previous rule).

nodes.label: C-7-06
nodes.text: A publisher MAY prepend a rendered citation or lineage line to `<description>` so that plain RSS readers see what the item answers or descends from; that line is presentation, exactly like the injected transclusion-provenance line, and is not part of `content_html`.

nodes.label: C-7-07
nodes.text: `<description>` HTML MUST be self-contained — which `content_html` already is (§5.2: every URL absolute) — with no dependence on the origin's stylesheets or scripts.

nodes.label: C-7-08
nodes.text: When an item's `author.name` is present, the publisher SHOULD emit `<dc:creator>` (`xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"`) with the display name — the standard RSS byline.

nodes.label: C-7-09
nodes.text: Publishers MUST emit it.

nodes.label: C-8-01
nodes.text: Once pinned, the file MUST return 200 forever — including after the item is withdrawn.

nodes.label: C-8-02
nodes.text: Any published version with content MAY be pinned, including retroactively (exposing withheld history is the publisher's right).

nodes.label: C-8-03
nodes.text: Withdrawal endcaps (§9) MUST NOT be pinned — there is nothing to cite.

nodes.label: C-8-04
nodes.text: **Media referenced by any pinned version MUST be retained forever.**

nodes.label: C-8-05
nodes.text: A pinned file SHOULD carry the assertion as published with that version, but both serve-time and publish-time assertion strategies are conformant.

nodes.label: C-8.4-01
nodes.text: The same rule bounds what a public page's version display may offer: every version it exposes — as a link, or presented in place — MUST be one the origin already promises forever, i.e. the live version and pinned versions, nothing else.

nodes.label: C-8.4-02
nodes.text: A version display MUST NOT offer, imply, or hint at access to unpinned history.

nodes.label: C-8.4-03
nodes.text: The floor is discrete pin citations (e.g. "v6 · pinned: v2, v4"); a page MAY additionally present the pinned artifacts themselves in place (the reference client pages among them with each shown version visibly marked frozen).

nodes.label: C-8.4-04
nodes.text: Additionally, a publisher **MAY** serve a rendered page for each pinned version at the item's permalink path plus a version segment:

nodes.label: C-8.4-05
nodes.text: The page SHOULD carry `rel="canonical"` pointing at the live permalink, SHOULD be visibly marked as a frozen snapshot, and SHOULD link its `v{n}.json` twin — the page is the human citation, the JSON the machine citation.

nodes.label: C-8.4-06
nodes.text: Pinned pages are **not** publish events: they MUST NOT appear in `feed.xml`, the archive index, or `items/index.json`, and they add no manifest vocabulary.

nodes.label: C-8.4-07
nodes.text: Readers MUST NOT require these pages — the subscribe side works entirely from the JSON surfaces.

nodes.label: C-9-01
nodes.text: A withdrawn stub stops *verifying* as a stub, because its endcap omits `stub_of`, and SHOULD re-send its mention once so the target learns this (§15.2).

nodes.label: C-10.1-01
nodes.text: `![[id@vN]]` (explicit version) is **reserved**: 0.3 publishers MUST reject it at publish time; readers MUST tolerate it as an unknown construct.

nodes.label: C-10.2-01
nodes.text: Each directive MUST resolve, in this order, to:

nodes.label: C-10.2-02
nodes.text: A directive with an attached blockquote (§10.1) resolves exactly as a whole directive — same order, same snapshot rule — and adds one check: at publish, the selection MUST be a substring of the target snapshot's **text content** — its `content_html` with tags stripped, whitespace collapsed within a block, block boundaries kept as line breaks — at the version being baked; otherwise a publish error, as for an unresolvable directive.

nodes.label: C-10.2-03
nodes.text: Any reader MAY re-check by the same test while the origin serves that version, live or pinned.

nodes.label: C-10.2-04
nodes.text: A thread MUST NOT transclude a local thread whose transitive *local* transclusion closure (walked via stored `transclusions[]`) contains the publishing thread's own id.

nodes.label: C-10.2-05
nodes.text: A studio SHOULD say at publish when a directive resolves to an unpinned remote item.

nodes.label: C-10.3-01
nodes.text: A partial transclusion's entry (§10.1, §10.2) additionally carries an OPTIONAL `selector` (revision of 2026-10-03, decision #49): `exact` REQUIRED — the selection, normalized by §10.2's text-content rule — `prefix` and `suffix` OPTIONAL and short; the W3C Web Annotation text-quote shape.

nodes.label: C-10.3-02
nodes.text: A remote entry is a **remote reference** and SHOULD send a mention to its origin (§15.2), whose relation is `transclusion`.

nodes.label: C-10.3-03
nodes.text: Readers at L2 MUST scope a transclusion's `id` to its `origin` when present, and to the document's own origin when absent, before doing anything with it — the same origin-scoping rule as everywhere else (§13.1).

nodes.label: C-10.6-01
nodes.text: A thread document MAY carry a top-level `"stub_of"`, in one of two shapes:

nodes.label: C-10.6-02
nodes.text: for a blyg target — a reference (§5.9), `origin` REQUIRED even when it is the publisher's own, because a citation is absolute — or

nodes.label: C-10.6-03
nodes.text: At publish, if the body transcludes the stub's target, `stub_of.version` MUST equal the version actually baked (§10.3); otherwise it keeps the value set when the stub was created — what the author saw.

nodes.label: C-10.6-04
nodes.text: A blyg-target stub is a **remote reference** when its origin is not the publisher's own, and SHOULD send a mention (§15.2), whose relation is `stub`.

nodes.label: C-10.6-05
nodes.text: A `{url}` stub SHOULD send an ordinary W3C Webmention to that URL if the target advertises an endpoint; most will not.

nodes.label: C-11-01
nodes.text: *(OPTIONAL at every level.)* The blogroll is the protocol's **static discovery plane**: a curated, published list of subscriptions the publisher chose to show.

nodes.label: C-11-02
nodes.text: The manifest advertises the file via the OPTIONAL `blogroll` key (§6.1).

nodes.label: C-11-03
nodes.text: Publishers SHOULD also emit `<link rel="blogroll" href="…">` on the HTML feed page.

nodes.label: C-11-04
nodes.text: It is whatever subset of their reading the publisher chose to publish; readers and crawlers MUST NOT treat it as a statement of everything the publisher follows.

nodes.label: C-11-05
nodes.text: Clients SHOULD treat inclusion as opt-in per subscription, defaulting to excluded — publishing a reading choice is a deliberate act.

nodes.label: C-12-01
nodes.text: Readers that subscribe MUST implement the following procedure in this order.

nodes.label: C-12.1-01
nodes.text: HTTPS is expected; readers MAY permit `http:` (local development) but SHOULD warn.

nodes.label: C-12.1-02
nodes.text: Readers MUST support the HTML `<link>` element here; supporting an equivalent HTTP `Link` header is OPTIONAL.

nodes.label: C-12.1-03
nodes.text: (Publishers whose blyg mounts away from their front page SHOULD emit this link on pages they expect to be shared.)

nodes.label: C-12.1-04
nodes.text: This is a courtesy fallback only — publishers MUST NOT rely on it.

nodes.label: C-12.1-05
nodes.text: Otherwise resolution fails, and the reader SHOULD report the trail of URLs tried.

nodes.label: C-12.2-01
nodes.text: If `site` disagrees with the fetch origin, the reader SHOULD surface the discrepancy and MUST NOT adopt the asserted value as identity — otherwise a mirror could inherit another origin's identity, violating origin scoping (§13.1).

nodes.label: C-12.2-02
nodes.text: **Redirects:** follow a bounded number (RECOMMENDED: 5); the *final* URL wins as origin.

nodes.label: C-12.2-03
nodes.text: **Re-resolution:** readers MAY re-run resolution when a subscription's surfaces 404 persistently (the blyg may have moved and left a rel link).

nodes.label: C-12.2-04
nodes.text: Adopting a new origin is an **identity change** and MUST be user-confirmed, never automatic.

nodes.label: C-12.3-01
nodes.text: Readers SHOULD poll with conditional requests (`If-None-Match` / `If-Modified-Since`) and honor `304`.

nodes.label: C-12.3-02
nodes.text: Readers SHOULD back off exponentially on repeated failure, SHOULD honor `Retry-After` on 429/503, and MUST NOT tighten their polling interval in response to failure.

nodes.label: C-12.3-03
nodes.text: Readers SHOULD send an identifying `User-Agent`, and the reference client derives its user agent from its `generator` string.

nodes.label: C-13.1-01
nodes.text: MUST treat item documents as ground truth and the feed as a lossy signal.

nodes.label: C-13.1-02
nodes.text: MUST roll up by `blyg:id`: highest `version` wins; ties are broken by `updated`.

nodes.label: C-13.1-03
nodes.text: MUST treat a withdrawal endcap as roll-up-to-null (§13.4).

nodes.label: C-13.1-04
nodes.text: MUST ignore unknown kinds, unknown JSON members, unknown `blyg:*` XML elements, and reserved constructs, without rejecting the containing document.

nodes.label: C-13.1-05
nodes.text: MUST NOT reject an item over its `author` contents, and MUST NOT treat equal `author` values from different origins as the same entity (§5.5).

nodes.label: C-13.1-06
nodes.text: SHOULD backfill from `items/index.json` when the feed window has been missed; a reader offline for any duration recovers losslessly.

nodes.label: C-13.1-07
nodes.text: MUST scope everything it learns to the origin: ids, authors, and trust do not transfer across origins.

nodes.label: C-13.1-08
nodes.text: MUST NOT gate any behaviour on `generator` or `level` (§3.2).

nodes.label: C-13.2-01
nodes.text: Readers SHOULD also reconcile against the index periodically regardless of suspicion (it is one file).

nodes.label: C-13.2-02
nodes.text: Poll failures of any kind MUST NOT alter stored item state.

nodes.label: C-13.2-03
nodes.text: A 404 on `items/index.json` from an otherwise-live blyg is a nonconforming publisher: readers SHOULD fall back to feed-window-only operation and surface the subscription as lossy.

nodes.label: C-13.3-01
nodes.text: The reader MUST NOT silently adopt it, SHOULD surface the discrepancy, and MAY offer a **user-confirmed** reset to origin state.

nodes.label: C-13.3-02
nodes.text: Content ground truth wins: the reader SHOULD adopt the fetched content, but SHOULD record and surface the discrepancy.

nodes.label: C-13.3-03
nodes.text: Readers SHOULD verify `content_hash` against `content_md` on import.

nodes.label: C-13.4-01
nodes.text: On a withdrawal endcap, a conforming reader rolls the item up to null: it MUST stop presenting the withdrawn content as live and SHOULD delete its stored copy — with one principled exception.

nodes.label: C-13.4-02
nodes.text: **Retention follows the origin's own serving surface**: content corresponding to a version the origin has **pinned** (a fetchable `items/{id}/v{n}.json`) MAY be retained and continue to be displayed, with attribution linking the pin — the origin itself still serves those exact bytes forever (§8.1), so local retention never exceeds the origin's own promise.

nodes.label: C-13.5-01
nodes.text: A client that both subscribes and publishes MUST keep the two planes separate:

nodes.label: C-13.5-02
nodes.text: They MUST NOT appear in the publisher's `feed.xml`, `items/index.json`, or as `items/{id}.json` documents, in any form — re-emission would collide with `blyg:id` rollup and break the single-publisher invariant (§5.5).

nodes.label: C-13.5-03
nodes.text: A client MAY **display** imported content publicly as curation — a shown list, with source attribution and links to the origin — without any protocol surface: no manifest vocabulary, no feed events, no new item documents.

nodes.label: C-13.5-04
nodes.text: A site that wants to present a group of blygs in one place is a reader with a public face: it displays curated imported content under this rule, publishes a blogroll of the members (§11) so any blyg-aware reader can subscribe to all of them in one import, and MAY serve a plain RSS digest *outside* the blyg surface — excerpts and links to origin permalinks, no `blyg:` namespace — for legacy readers that want one feed.

nodes.label: C-13.6-01
nodes.text: Synthetic ids are never valid blyg ids and MUST NOT be exported or re-emitted in any protocol surface.

nodes.label: C-13.6-02
nodes.text: Clients SHOULD mark L0 items visibly as wrapped legacy content.

nodes.label: C-13.7-01
nodes.text: Readers SHOULD ensure a skewed or future-dated origin cannot permanently dominate the display order.

nodes.label: C-14-01
nodes.text: This is the same standing as every other self-asserted claim above, and readers SHOULD present remote quotes as *the publisher's snapshot of* the source, not as the source.

nodes.label: C-14-02
nodes.text: The reference implementation renders markdown with raw HTML escaped and sanitizes imported HTML before baking it, but readers MUST sanitize or sandbox fetched `content_html` before rendering it in their own UI, as with any syndicated HTML, and MUST NOT assume a nested snapshot was sanitized by anyone.

nodes.label: C-14-03
nodes.text: Server-side readers SHOULD apply standard fetch hygiene: bounded redirects (§12.2), response size and time limits, and refusal to fetch private-network addresses where the deployment could be used to probe them.

nodes.label: C-15-01
nodes.text: *(New in 0.3. OPTIONAL at every level.)* The blogroll (§11) is the static half of discovery: who a publisher chose to show they read.

nodes.label: C-15.1-01
nodes.text: Permalink pages and the feed page SHOULD carry `<link rel="webmention" href="…">` and SHOULD announce the endpoint in an HTTP `Link` header, per W3C discovery, so that non-blyg senders find it.

nodes.label: C-15.2-01
nodes.text: A publisher SHOULD send a mention for each **remote reference** in a newly published version: every blyg-target `stub_of` whose origin is not its own (§10.6), every `transclusions[]` entry carrying an `origin` (§10.3), and a `forked_from` naming another origin (§5.6).

nodes.label: C-15.2-02
nodes.text: A `{url}` stub SHOULD send an ordinary Webmention to that URL.

nodes.label: C-15.2-03
nodes.text: A network failure or 5xx is retried with backoff — RECOMMENDED 15 minutes, 1 hour, 4 hours, 12 hours, 24 hours — then abandoned. 4xx is terminal, except 429, which retries.

nodes.label: C-15.2-04
nodes.text: Delivery is **fire-and-forget from the author's point of view**: publish MUST NOT block on it, and outbound status is information, never a publish outcome.

nodes.label: C-15.3-01
nodes.text: Both MUST be absolute `http(s)` URLs; `source` MUST differ from `target`; `target`'s origin (scheme, host, port) MUST be this blyg's own, and its path MUST name a published item — by `page`, or as `items/{id}.json`.

nodes.label: C-15.3-02
nodes.text: RECOMMENDED: more than 60 mentions from one source host in an hour.

nodes.label: C-15.3-03
nodes.text: Receivers SHOULD therefore also cap by a coarser grouping of the source (the reference client groups by registrable domain, at a looser limit than the per-host one, because the grouping is a heuristic that can over-collect) and cap total accepted claims per hour regardless of source.

nodes.label: C-15.4-01
nodes.text: Verification is bounded — RECOMMENDED: at most 2 fetches, at most 3 redirects, 5 seconds per fetch, 1 MB per body — and these bounds are the receiver's protection, not a nicety (§14).

nodes.label: C-15.4-02
nodes.text: If it is HTML, find `<link rel="alternate" type="application/json">` (§5.8) and fetch that; it MUST be a blyg item document.

nodes.label: C-15.4-03
nodes.text: **The document's `origin` MUST equal the final source URL's origin** (scheme, host, port; trailing slash normalized).

nodes.label: C-15.4-04
nodes.text: A mention that verified before and fails now becomes **gone**; the receiver SHOULD keep the record with that status rather than deleting it, so that a stubber who withdraws and later republishes is recognized rather than treated as new.

nodes.label: C-15.5-01
nodes.text: A publisher MAY display verified mentions of an item publicly — a "responses" list on a permalink page — and if it does, that is **per-item curation** under §13.5: a shown list with attribution and links to the origin, publicity being a property of the list, never of the mention.

nodes.label: C-15.6-01
nodes.text: A receiver MAY accept mentions whose source is not a blyg item document, verified the W3C way (the source page contains the target URL), and if it does MUST hold them **apart** from structurally verified mentions as a lower class — never in the same signal, never displayed as a response — because link verification is exactly the check that trackback spam defeated.

nodes.label: P-16.1a-01
nodes.text: **Ruled: a `{url}` stub (§10.6) MAY carry the same `cited` object**, under §5.9's rules unchanged — `retrieved` REQUIRED, self-asserted, frozen when the stub was created, ignored by verification, never baked, ignorable by any reader, `excerpt` a caption capped near 200 characters — entering §10.6 once a client emits it and an import across nodes retains it (decision #55, on [blygger-spec#7](https://github.com/blygger/blygger-spec/issues/7)). §10.2's "plain-web targets get nothing" is about *verification*: a selector promises a faithfulness test that cannot run against a page with no versioned document.

nodes.label: P-16.1a-02
nodes.text: `cited` promises no test — §15.4 MUST ignore it and a reader that drops it stays conformant — and §5.9's own argument is *stronger* for a target that cannot be re-fetched at any version: the citing publisher's frozen label is the only record of what was read.

nodes.label: P-16.3-01
nodes.text: **Ruled 2026-09-28: a generator MAY be fed another origin's words, and that is a *source*, not a quotation, disclosed as a reference — and it notifies.** §5.7 rule 3's line between the two authorial acts, verbatim-and-visible versus drawn-upon-and-woven, does not move when the words come from another origin; a blockquote around non-verbatim prose would be false.

nodes.label: P-16.3-02
nodes.text: `sources[]` takes the reference shape of §5.9 — `origin` omitted for own-origin, present for remote — and MAY carry `cited`.

nodes.label: P-16.3-03
nodes.text: A remote source is a **remote reference** and SHOULD send a mention (§15.2) whose relation is **`source`** — a fourth relation, added to §15.4's set when this construct enters normative text.

nodes.label: P-16.4-01
nodes.text: The wish behind the question — a leading heading shown as the item's linked title — needs nothing from the wire: the RECOMMENDED derivation's excerpt half already begins with the heading when there is one, and how a client renders its own pages is presentation. §5.3's reader rule stands: readers MUST NOT extract a title from content, because a reader inventing structure the publisher did not assert is the failure that rule exists to prevent.

nodes.label: P-16.5-01
nodes.text: A client MAY show, as presentation, that an item it quotes has itself gone stale on something — the nested `data-blyg-*` attributes (§10.2) plus one fetch per layer are enough — but that is a reading aid, not staleness of the quoting document.

nodes.label: P-16.6b-01
nodes.text: An agent's byline SHOULD name an operator; that convention lives in the identity note.

nodes.label: P-16.6c-01
nodes.text: **Ruled 2026-09-28: a changelog entry MAY carry `"generated": true`**, meaning the publisher's studio wrote the note (from the local diff between versions) rather than the author.

nodes.label: P-16.6c-02
nodes.text: Self-asserted and unverifiable like `generated[]` (§5.7 rule 6); absent means only "not stated"; readers MUST NOT gate on it.

nodes.label: P-16.6d-01
nodes.text: A reader MAY walk these — the chain in a snapshot, the `stub_of` chain to its root, its own verified mentions, its subscriptions' blogrolls — and MAY order what it finds by any local heuristic, provided nothing derived is published (the no-metrics rule).

nodes.label: P-16.6d-02
nodes.text: *Forward* discovery — who has responded to an item you did not publish — is deliberately not on the wire: verified mentions are studio signals (§15.5), and a publisher's public responses list is presentation that readers MUST NOT parse as protocol.

nodes.label: P-16.6d-03
nodes.text: **Considered for 0.4 and kept closed (2026-09-28):** an OPTIONAL per-item curated responses surface in the blogroll's shape — opt-in per item, structurally verified sources only, no completeness claim, never re-emitting content.

nodes.label: P-16.6e-01
nodes.text: **Two OPTIONAL template keys**, in [RFC 6570](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6570) level-1 form: `item` (variable `id`, default `items/{id}.json`) and `pin` (variables `id` and `n`, default `items/{id}/v{n}.json`).

nodes.label: P-16.6e-02
nodes.text: Readers MUST expand them wherever this document says `{origin}items/{id}.json` or `{origin}items/{id}/v{n}.json`.

nodes.label: P-16.6e-03
nodes.text: **`page` MAY be absolute** (§5.8), since a CMS permalink lives outside the surface's mount; media URLs already may be (§5.4).

nodes.label: P-16.6f-01
nodes.text: The `blyg-transclusion` class MUST NOT survive into the fork: the forking publisher baked nothing and verified nothing.
